output.body:
# HIU, health information user

## In plain words

A health information user is the side of an exchange that wants records it
does not hold. It is identified by a service id, carried in the `X-HIU-ID`
header, which the specification describes as:

> Identifier of the health information user to which the request was intended

The same organisation often holds both roles, one for the records it keeps
and one for the records it wants to read.

## Before you start

You need a consent request the patient has approved, because this role reads
nothing without one.

## What happens

`m3_post_consent_v3_request_init` raises the consent request that this role
begins every exchange with.

## How you know it worked

You have understood this when you can say which role a consent request is
raised by and which role it is served against.

## When it goes wrong

Requesting health information on a consent artefact that has expired or been
revoked, which the specification states must not be done.

reply.Text:
**HIU** stands for **Health Information User**. It's one of the two key roles in ABDM's health data exchange.

From the [ABDM glossary](https://abdm-developer.nha.gov.in/docs/hiecm/v3/getting-started/glossary#hiu):

A health information user is a system that:
- **Requests health records it doesn't hold** — it's the side of an exchange that wants to read records from elsewhere
- **Gets patient consent first** — HIUs must have the patient's approved consent before fetching any records
- **Is identified by a service ID** — carried in the `X-HIU-ID` header

The same organization often holds both roles simultaneously: one as a **HIP** (Health Information Provider, for records it keeps) and one as an **HIU** (for records it wants to read).

When things go wrong, the most common issue is requesting health information on an expired or revoked consent artefact.
